Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0003] Read the target module and tests before editing: Start by reading the file to be modified, related models/utilities, and any existing tests for the feature to align signatures and behavior.
  Cat invoice.py, models.py, money.py, and tests/test_average_unit_price.py before writing code. This reveals the exact stub signature, dataclass field names (line.quantity, line.unit_price), and expected return type, enabling a first-attempt pass.
- [rb-0002] Guard division with a zero-total check: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator before dividing and return the documented fallback (ZERO) when it is zero.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it is falsy, return ZERO immediately. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement and avoids ZeroDivisionError without try/except.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal math: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and models.py first to learn the money policy. Wrap inputs with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round results with round_money so rounding and type conventions match the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Match existing error codes and validation patterns before implementing
item.description: Grep the codebase for similar validation (state checks, amount checks) to reuse established BillingError codes and message formats.
item.content: Before writing validation logic, search for existing patterns like `invalid_state` or `negative_amount` in sibling modules. Reusing the same error codes and f-string message formats keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on codes.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer types
item.description: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(x, int) accepts True/False; explicitly reject bools for integer-only parameters.
item.content: When a parameter must be a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before the range check. Otherwise True would pass as quantity 1 and silently corrupt data.

item.title: Normalize money inputs through the project's to_money helper
item.description: Convert raw unit_price values with the existing to_money/round_money utilities before comparing or storing, rather than assuming Decimal.
item.content: Call `to_money(unit_price)` to coerce inputs, then compare against the module's ZERO constant for negativity. This handles ints, strings, and Decimals uniformly and keeps stored LineItem values consistent with the rest of the codebase.
